summary: Battle City top-down tank slice designed as a complete package: game-design.json (2 actions, 7 entities, 11 rules, win/lose conditions closed over existing ids), style-guide.json (320x240 logical, 16px tiles/sprites, monochrome palette, N/E/S/W, 2-16 fps, nearest filtering), three 12x12 levels, asset-requirements.json (13 requirements covering every entity plus all non-floor/non-decor tiles: b, x, w, h, g, t), and acceptance-plan.json (22 items spanning design/assets/engine/playtest/human). Difficulty ramps per the template: level_1 "Training Yard" teaches movement only to an exit at (9,10) with no enemies; level_2 "Brick Breakthrough" puts the exit at (6,0) behind a brick lattice so shooting carves a shortcut; level_3 "River Siege" adds 3 enemy tanks, water corridors, steel cover, 2 hazard tiles and base defense. Every stage exit was hand-verified walkable from spawn on non-blocking tiles, and no spawn sits on a blocking tile.
risks: explosion is authored as entity kind 'prop' because the contract's kind enum lacks 'effect' (the genre template uses it); it maps to an 'effect' asset requirement. If the schema gains 'effect', this should be migrated.

game-design.json scope must be numeric-only: the validator rejects booleans (expected u32), so all scope values are integers (levels, grid_w/h, tile_size_px, sprite_size_px, logical_width/height, max_players, screens_per_stage) rather than flags.
hq_base sits on a non-blocking floor tile, so it must be rendered as a prop overlay rather than an occupancy tile; enemy bullet collision with the base needs a dedicated hitbox in engine.

level_3 enemies (9,5), (4,9), (10,3) all stand on floor but (10,3) is directly above hazard (11,3) — engine patrol logic must not push a tank onto a hazard-adjacent lane carelessly, or the stage may feel unfair.
Stage 2 and 3 exits are reachable without firing by design; if designers prefer shooting to be mandatory, the open bypass lane should be closed.
open_questions: Should the HQ base destruction be survivable on level_3 (respawn/lives) or an instant stage loss as specified?
Is a hazard tile ('h') wanted at all on level_3, given the brief lists water but not hazards as an element?
Should grass ('t') render above tanks for the classic occlusive look, or below them for clarity?
